reasoning_traces.think:
Hierarchical stacking generalizes standard stacking by replacing fixed weight vectors with input-dependent weight functions w(x). This allows models to be selectively applied in regions where they are locally optimal, addressing the issue of global model misfit. The method uses a Bayesian formulation with a LOO objective that avoids data reuse while enabling posterior inference. The hierarchical prior on weights introduces shrinkage, which is particularly useful in low-sample regimes such as early NFL seasons. The softmax parameterization ensures that weights remain normalized and interpretable. The resulting pointwise weights w(x) enable GSE to make regime-specific ensemble decisions, while GSI benefits from improved predictive uncertainty through PSIS-LOO diagnostics. The theoretical framework provides bounds on performance gains over model selection and complete pooling, showing that stacking excels when models are locally separated but no single model dominates globally.
